plan.reason.base: Volume in the low zones and one quality session a week. This is the base the harder weeks before {goal} rest on.
plan.reason.build: The quality sessions grow, with threshold intervals and hard intervals, while the rest stays easy.
plan.reason.peak: The time right before the taper. The volume stands still and the sessions resemble {goal} in pace and length.
plan.reason.taper: The last stretch before {goal}: the volume drops to about half and the speed stays in short efforts, so that you start rested.
plan.reason.base_cycle: Volume in the low zones and one quality session a week, on the way to the test in week {test_week}.
plan.reason.build_cycle: Longer quality sessions. The block ends with a new test in week {test_week}, which shows what the training gave and sets new zones.
plan.note.short: There are only {weeks} weeks to the goal. The plan therefore builds no peak: it keeps your fitness and tapers for the race.
plan.note.capped: You train more today than the times you gave can hold. The plan stays within those times, at most {minutes} minutes a week.
plan.note.goal_outside: {name} lies outside the weeks of the plan and is not included.
plan.note.no_test: The plan is not built on a test. The sessions therefore give the zone and the effort, without heart rate and pace.
plan.note.estimated: The zones are estimated from max heart rate, since no thresholds are measured. A lactate test gives your own borders and a pace per zone.
plan.note.speed_from_hr: The zones are estimated from max heart rate, since no thresholds are measured. The pace comes from the relation between heart rate and speed in the zones test, not from lactate. ≈ means the pace lies a little outside the steps of the test. A lactate test gives your own borders.
plan.error.no_slots: State at least one day a week when training is possible.
plan.error.goal_too_close: {name} is too close to the start date. A plan needs at least two weeks.
plan.error.too_short: A plan without a goal is at least {weeks} weeks.
plan.week.focus.base: Load week in the base block: plenty of easy running and one quality session. Keep the easy runs easy.
plan.week.focus.build: Load week in the build block: the quality sessions matter most this week, and the days between them are easy.
plan.week.focus.peak: Peak week: the volume stands still and the sessions resemble the race. Sleep and eat as before a race.
plan.week.focus.easy: Easy week: about two thirds of the volume, so that the body can absorb the training. Do not add anything.
plan.week.focus.test: Test week: an easy week with a new test at your coach. After the test every session gets new targets in heart rate and pace.
plan.week.focus.taper: Taper: shorter sessions, the same pace in short efforts. Fitness is no longer built, it is brought out.
plan.week.focus.race: Race week: short, easy runs and one short session with pace early in the week. Rest the day or days before the start.
plan.week.race_a: {name} this week: two easy days before and after the race.
plan.week.race_b: Milestone: {name}. The week is lighter, the last quality session lies at least three days before and two easy days follow.
plan.week.race_c: Training race: {name}. It replaces one of the week's quality sessions.
plan.workout.easy.title: Easy run
plan.workout.easy.purpose: Builds endurance without wearing you down. Most of the training should look like this.
plan.workout.easy.how: Even, easy pace at which you can talk in full sentences. If the heart rate passes zone 2 on a hill: slow down or walk.
plan.workout.recovery.title: Recovery jog
plan.workout.recovery.purpose: Helps the body absorb yesterday's session. You should feel better after than before.
plan.workout.recovery.how: Short and very easy, in the lower part of zone 2. If the legs feel heavy: shorten the run or walk.
plan.workout.long.title: Long run
plan.workout.long.purpose: The key endurance session of the week: teaches the body to work long on fat and strengthens muscles and tendons.
plan.workout.long.how: Easy all the way, rather too slow than too fast. Bring a drink on runs over an hour.
plan.workout.long_progressive.title: Long run with a fast finish
plan.workout.long_progressive.purpose: Gets the body used to race pace on tired legs.
plan.workout.long_progressive.how: Easy like a normal long run, and the last 20 minutes in zone 3: brisk but controlled.
plan.workout.threshold.title: Threshold intervals
plan.workout.threshold.purpose: Moves the threshold up: you can hold a higher pace for longer.
plan.workout.threshold.how: Just below the threshold, hard but controlled. You should be able to say a few words and manage one more interval when you finish. Jog or walk in the rests.
plan.workout.vo2max.title: Hard intervals
plan.workout.vo2max.purpose: Raises the maximal oxygen uptake, the ceiling of your fitness.
plan.workout.vo2max.how: Hard and even: the same pace in the first and the last interval. The heart rate reaches zone 5 only some way into the interval, so go by pace and feel at first.
plan.workout.fartlek.title: Fartlek
plan.workout.fartlek.purpose: Speed in a playful form: gets the body used to threshold pace without the wear of intervals.
plan.workout.fartlek.how: Pick up to threshold effort in the surges and jog easily between them without stopping.
plan.workout.hills.title: Hill repeats
plan.workout.hills.purpose: Strength and stride: power in the push-off with little impact on the legs.
plan.workout.hills.how: An even hill with a moderate slope. Strong uphill with a tall posture and short steps, an easy jog down as rest.
plan.workout.opener.title: Pre-race session
plan.workout.opener.purpose: Keeps the speed awake without tiring you.
plan.workout.opener.how: Short efforts at race feel with long rests. You should want to run more when you finish.
plan.workout.test.title: Test at your coach
plan.workout.test.purpose: Shows what the training has given and sets new zones. Every coming session gets new targets in heart rate and pace.
plan.workout.test.how: Come rested: an easy day before, no hard training for two days, the same food and drink as before the last test.
plan.workout.race.title: Race
plan.workout.race.purpose: This is the day the plan leads up to.
plan.workout.race.how: Warm up easily, start under control and save your strength for the second half.
plan.ics.name: Training plan {name}
plan.pdf.title: Training plan
plan.pdf.kicker_test: Training plan built on your test
plan.pdf.fact.no_goal: No race: the plan ends with a new test that shows the progress
plan.pdf.tile.volume_sub: grows by at most 10 % a week
plan.pdf.tile.easy_sub: of the time in zones 1–2, below the aerobic threshold
plan.pdf.overview.title: The blocks and the weeks
plan.start.recent: Starts at {start} a week, what you train now.
plan.start.default: Starts at {start} a week, the level's default since Trains now is empty.
plan.start.capped: Starts at {start} a week, all the time the days can hold.
plan.start.grows: The time grows to {top} in week {week}.
plan.start.flat: The time stands still, so the progression lies in the sessions: the longest run and the hard minutes.
plan.pdf.lines.title: Longest run and hard minutes, per week
plan.pdf.zones.title: Your zones
plan.pdf.zones.sub: heart rate in bpm and pace from your test
plan.pdf.zones.estimated_hr: estimated from max heart rate, pace from heart rate
plan.pdf.zones.none: without a test only the zone and the effort are given
plan.pdf.zones.note: The plan states zones, not numbers. Heart rate and pace here and on the week sheets come from your latest test, and after a new test the sheets are printed with new values. Pace is given only where the test measured it.
plan.pdf.promise.title: How to use the plan.
plan.pdf.promise.text: Every session has a zone with heart rate and pace from your own test. Do the sessions as written, keep the easy runs easy and tick them off on the week sheet. A missed session is not made up.
plan.pdf.read.title: How to read the plan
plan.pdf.read.lead: The plan is built with fixed rules from your test, your times and your goal. Here is why the blocks lie where they do, what the zones mean for you and how the sessions should feel.
plan.pdf.blocks.title: The blocks
plan.pdf.guide.title: The sessions in the plan
plan.pdf.rules.title: The rules behind the plan
plan.pdf.rule.1: Most of it is easy: about four fifths of the time lies below the aerobic threshold, and at most a quarter of a week above it.
plan.pdf.rule.2: Never two hard days in a row, and never a hard session the day before the long run.
plan.pdf.rule.3: A week is never more than 10 % bigger than the biggest week before it, and the long run grows by at most 15 minutes at a time.
plan.pdf.rule.4: After two or three load weeks comes an easy week, where the body absorbs the training.
plan.pdf.rule.5: The plan never raises anything by itself. New targets in heart rate and pace only come from a new test, and changes are made by your coach.
plan.pdf.rule.6: If you miss a session: skip it. If you are ill with a fever or symptoms below the neck: rest, and start again gently.
plan.pdf.disclaimer: The plan is training advice built on a test, not health care. It does not replace a doctor or a physiotherapist. If you get chest pain, dizziness or abnormal shortness of breath: stop the session and seek care.
plan.pdf.overview.sketch: Sketch: the workouts come four weeks at a time
plan.pdf.sketch.title: The sketch
plan.pdf.sketch.lead: The workouts run to week {week} ({date}). The weeks after are a sketch: block, kind of week, time and number of sessions. The workouts come four weeks at a time when the plan is renewed.
plan.note.borrowed.ski: The ski sessions use the SkiErg's heart rate zones, since there is no test on skis. Watt and time per 500 m apply on the SkiErg only.
plan.note.no_test_sport.bike: The cycling sessions are not built on a cycling test and give the zone and the effort.
plan.note.no_test_sport.skierg: The SkiErg sessions are not built on a SkiErg test and give the zone and the effort.
plan.note.no_test_sport.ski: The ski sessions are not built on a test and give the zone and the effort.
plan.note.no_test_sport.swim: The swimming sessions give the zone and the perceived effort (RPE), since there is no swim test.
plan.workout.bike_easy.title: easy Z2 ride
plan.workout.bike_easy.purpose: Builds endurance with little load on the legs. Most of the time on the bike should look like this.
plan.workout.bike_easy.how: Even, light pedalling at a cadence around 85–95 rpm. Keep the watt and the heart rate in zone 2, also on the hills: shift down rather than stand up.
plan.workout.bike_recovery.title: recovery ride
plan.workout.bike_recovery.purpose: Gets the legs moving and helps the body absorb yesterday's session.
plan.workout.bike_recovery.how: Very light resistance and light pedalling, in the lower part of zone 2 or below.
plan.workout.bike_long.title: long ride
plan.workout.bike_long.purpose: The long session of the week: endurance and fat burning with less wear than a long run.
plan.workout.bike_long.how: Easy all the way in zone 2. Eat and drink a little at a time from the first hour.
plan.workout.bike_long_progressive.title: long ride with a fast finish
plan.workout.bike_long_progressive.purpo: Gets the body used to race effort on tired legs.
plan.workout.bike_long_progressive.how: Easy like a normal long ride, and the last 20 minutes in zone 3: even pressure, under control.
plan.workout.bike_sweetspot.title: sweet spot
plan.workout.bike_sweetspot.purpose: Long blocks just below the threshold: a lot of threshold training at a small cost in fatigue.
plan.workout.bike_sweetspot.how: Hold the watt at 88–94 % of your threshold power, evenly through the block. That is the session's target in watt; the heart rate ends up in the lower part of zone 4 and drifts up a little during the block. Light pedalling between the blocks, cadence 85–95.
plan.workout.bike_threshold.title: threshold intervals
plan.workout.bike_threshold.purpose: Moves the threshold up: you can hold a higher watt for longer.
plan.workout.bike_threshold.how: Even watt in zone 4, hard but controlled. The last interval should be at the same watt as the first. Light pedalling in the rests.
plan.workout.bike_vo2max.title: VO2 intervals
plan.workout.bike_vo2max.purpose: Raises the maximal oxygen uptake, the ceiling of your fitness.
plan.workout.bike_vo2max.how: Hard and even in zone 5. Go by the watt from the start: the heart rate reaches the zone only some way into the interval. Light pedalling in the rests.
plan.workout.bike_vo2_short.title: short intervals
plan.workout.bike_vo2_short.purpose: A lot of time near the maximal heart rate in short pieces: raises the oxygen uptake without much wear.
plan.workout.bike_vo2_short.how: One minute hard in zone 5 and one minute of light pedalling. The same watt in every interval, preferably a higher cadence than usual (95–105).
plan.workout.bike_opener.title: pre-race session
plan.workout.bike_opener.purpose: Keeps the legs awake without tiring you.
plan.workout.bike_opener.how: Short efforts at race feel with long rests. You should want to ride more when you finish.
plan.workout.skierg_easy.title: easy session
plan.workout.skierg_easy.purpose: Builds endurance in the upper body and the core. Most of the time should look like this.
plan.workout.skierg_easy.how: Long, relaxed strokes at a low rate. Keep the heart rate in zone 2, on the SkiErg also the watt and the time per 500 m.
plan.workout.skierg_recovery.title: recovery session
plan.workout.skierg_recovery.purpose: Helps the body absorb yesterday's session.
plan.workout.skierg_recovery.how: Short and very easy, with light pressure in the stroke. If it feels heavy: shorten the session.
plan.workout.skierg_long.title: long session
plan.workout.skierg_long.purpose: The long session of the week: endurance for long races.
plan.workout.skierg_long.how: Easy all the way in zone 2. Vary the technique, and eat and drink on sessions over an hour.
plan.workout.skierg_long_progressive.tit: long session with a fast finish
plan.workout.skierg_long_progressive.pur: Gets the body used to race pace on tired arms and legs.
plan.workout.skierg_long_progressive.how: Easy like a normal long session, and the last 20 minutes in zone 3: brisk but controlled.
plan.workout.skierg_threshold.title: threshold intervals
plan.workout.skierg_threshold.purpose: Moves the threshold up: you can hold a higher pace for longer.
plan.workout.skierg_threshold.how: Just below the threshold in zone 4, hard but controlled. Even watt and time per 500 m through the interval. Light strokes or rest in the breaks.
plan.workout.skierg_vo2max.title: hard intervals
plan.workout.skierg_vo2max.purpose: Raises the maximal oxygen uptake, the ceiling of your fitness.
plan.workout.skierg_vo2max.how: Hard and even in zone 5: the same watt in the first and the last interval. The heart rate reaches the zone only some way in, so go by the watt and feel at first.
plan.workout.skierg_fartlek.title: fartlek
plan.workout.skierg_fartlek.purpose: Surges at threshold pace with easy strokes between: gets the body used to the threshold without the wear of intervals.
plan.workout.skierg_fartlek.how: Pick up to threshold effort in the surges and go on easily between them without stopping.
plan.workout.skierg_hills.title: short intervals
plan.workout.skierg_hills.purpose: Power and technique in the stroke: high pressure in short pieces.
plan.workout.skierg_hills.how: Powerful strokes with the whole body and a high rate. On skis: an even hill. Easy in the rests.
plan.workout.skierg_opener.title: pre-race session
plan.workout.skierg_opener.purpose: Keeps the speed awake without tiring you.
plan.workout.skierg_opener.how: Short efforts at race pace with long rests. You should want to go on when you finish.
plan.workout.long_progressive.title_any: long session with a faster finish
plan.workout.swim_easy.title: easy session
plan.workout.swim_easy.purpose: Builds endurance and ease in the water. Most of the swimming should look like this.
plan.workout.swim_easy.how: Even, easy swimming with long, relaxed strokes. Effort 3 of 10: you can breathe calmly every stroke or every other. Rest at the wall when the technique starts to fall apart.
plan.workout.swim_technique.title: technique session
plan.workout.swim_technique.purpose: Makes swimming cheaper: a better position in the water, longer strokes and calmer breathing. Also works as recovery.
plan.workout.swim_technique.how: Drills at an easy pace, for example 25 m drill and 25 m swim: side kick, single arm, catch-up and counting strokes per length. Effort 2–3 of 10. Quality before metres.
plan.workout.swim_long.title: long session
plan.workout.swim_long.purpose: The longest swim of the week: endurance and an even pace for a long time.
plan.workout.swim_long.how: Even and easy all the way, effort 4 of 10. Swim longer stretches without rest if you can, and keep the rests at the wall to a few breaths.
plan.workout.swim_long_progressive.title: long session with a faster finish
plan.workout.swim_long_progressive.purpo: Teaches the body to hold the pace when tired, as at the end of a race.
plan.workout.swim_long_progressive.how: Easy at first. The last 20 minutes just above easy, effort 6 of 10, without the technique falling apart.
plan.workout.swim_intervals.title: intervals
plan.workout.swim_intervals.purpose: Moves the threshold up in the water: you can hold a faster pace for longer.
plan.workout.swim_intervals.how: Even pace around the threshold, effort 7 of 10: hard but controlled, every interval as fast as the first. Rest at the wall between the intervals.
plan.workout.swim_hard.title: hard intervals
plan.workout.swim_hard.purpose: Raises the ceiling: oxygen uptake and speed in the water.
plan.workout.swim_hard.how: Faster than the threshold pace, effort 9 of 10. Keep the technique: if the strokes get short and hurried, slow down or rest longer.
plan.workout.swim_mixed.title: mixed pace
plan.workout.swim_mixed.purpose: Builds endurance at a pace between easy and threshold, with technique under light fatigue.
plan.workout.swim_mixed.how: Longer blocks at a steady pace, effort 6 of 10, with easy swimming between.
plan.workout.swim_sprints.title: short intervals
plan.workout.swim_sprints.purpose: Speed and power in the stroke, without getting tired for long.
plan.workout.swim_sprints.how: Short, fast lengths with good technique, effort 8 of 10, and as long a rest. It should feel fast, not heavy.
plan.workout.swim_opener.title: race opener
plan.workout.swim_opener.purpose: Keeps the speed in the body without tiring before the race.
plan.workout.swim_opener.how: A few short pieces at race pace, effort 6 of 10, with plenty of rest. Finish fresh.
plan.workout.strength_full.title: full body
plan.workout.strength_full.purpose: Makes muscles, tendons and joints stronger, so that they take more training and get injured less often.
plan.workout.strength_full.how: Legs, hips, core, back and shoulders, for example squats, deadlifts, lunges, push-ups, rows and planks. 2–3 sets of 6–12 repetitions, effort 7 of 10: two repetitions left in every set. No zones.
plan.workout.strength_legs.title: legs and core
plan.workout.strength_legs.purpose: Stronger legs, hips and core: a better running stride and pedal stroke, and fewer overuse injuries.
plan.workout.strength_legs.how: Squats, lunges, single-leg exercises, calf raises, hip thrusts and core exercises. 2–3 sets of 6–12 repetitions, effort 7 of 10. No zones. Heavy legs: take the next day easier.
plan.workout.strength_upper.title: upper body and mobility
plan.workout.strength_upper.purpose: A stronger back, shoulders and arms, and mobility in the hips and upper back, without tiring the legs.
plan.workout.strength_upper.how: Rows, push-ups, presses, chin-ups or pull-downs and core exercises, then mobility. 2–3 sets of 8–12 repetitions, effort 6 of 10. No zones.
plan.workout.strength_maintenance.title: maintenance
plan.workout.strength_maintenance.purpos: Keeps the strength until the goal without tiring.
plan.workout.strength_maintenance.how: The usual exercises but fewer sets and lighter weights, effort 5 of 10. No heavy loads in the last days before the goal.
plan.workout.bike_test.title: lactate test at your coach
plan.workout.bike_test.purpose: Shows what the training has given and sets new zones on the bike. Every coming ride gets new targets in heart rate and watt.
plan.workout.bike_test.how: A lactate step test on the trainer: 10 minutes of warm-up and then 6–8 steps of 5 minutes, 25–30 W more for each step, with a blood sample at the end of each step. Come rested: an easy day before, no hard training for two days, the same food and drink as before the last test. Bring your own cycling shoes and pedals if you have them.
plan.workout.skierg_test.title: lactate test at your coach
plan.workout.skierg_test.purpose: Shows what the training has given and sets new zones in double poling. Every coming session gets new targets in heart rate, watt and time per 500 m.
plan.workout.skierg_test.how: A lactate step test on the SkiErg: 10 minutes of warm-up and then 6–8 steps of 4 minutes, 15–20 W more for each step, with a blood sample in a half-minute pause after each step. Come rested: an easy day before, no hard training for two days, the same food and drink as before the last test.
plan.workout.ski_test.title: lactate test on the SkiErg at your coach
plan.workout.ski_test.purpose: Shows what the training has given and sets new heart rate zones for the ski sessions, which use the SkiErg's zones.
plan.workout.ski_test.how: The test is done on the SkiErg, since there is no test on skis: 10 minutes of warm-up and then 6–8 steps of 4 minutes, 15–20 W more for each step, with a blood sample in a half-minute pause after each step. Come rested: an easy day before, no hard training for two days, the same food and drink as before the last test.
plan.workout.swim_test.title: swim test, 400 m and 200 m
plan.workout.swim_test.purpose: Gives your threshold pace in the water (CSS). The swim sessions get a time per 100 m for each zone instead of effort only.
plan.workout.swim_test.how: Warm up for 15–20 minutes with a few short pick-ups. Swim 400 m as fast as you can at an even pace and take the time. Rest until you have fully recovered, at least 8–10 minutes of easy swimming. Then swim 200 m in the same way. The same pool and the same start (a push-off in the water) every time. Give the two times to your coach.
